 Order

Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 and learned counsel for respondent No.2.
2.

The second respondent lodged the First Information Report alleging that, she is the legally wedded wife of accused No.1 and at the time of marriage, her parents gave dowry to accused No.1 in the form of cash, jewelry, etc.

Accused Nos.2 to 11 are the relatives of accused No.1.
3.

It is the case of defacto-complainant is that, the petitioners-accused Nos.2 to 11 along with accused No.1 used to subject the second respondent to cruelty both mentally and physically and also demanded to bring additional dowry from her parental home.

On 24.05.2023 all the petitioners-accused and accused No.1 formed an unlawful assembly took quarrel with her, abused her and intentionally insulted and provoked her breach of peace and also made NC:
2024:KHC-D:8069 criminal intimidation to eliminate her.
Hence, on 30.05.2023 she lodged complaint to the Police.

The police after investigation, laid the charge sheet for the offences punishable under Sections 498(A),323, 504 and 506 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code (for short, 'the IPC') and 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act (for short, 'the D.P.Act').
4.
The learned Magistrate, after accepting the charge sheet, took cognizance of the aforesaid offences and issued summons.

Taking exception of the same, this petition is filed by accused Nos.2 to 11.
5.
Perused the charge sheet materials.
The defacto-complainant has specifically stated that she was thrown out from the matrimonial home in the month of May, 2023.
On 24.05.2023 the petitioners- accused Nos.2 to 11 along with accused No.1 took quarrel with her, abused her, assaulted her, and also made criminal intimidation to eliminate her.

From perusal of the entire materials on record, except omnibus and general allegations, there are no specific allegations made against petitioners as to how and in what manner they subjected to the defacto-complainant to cruelty both mentally and physically and also that there was a demand made to bring additional dowry from her parental home.

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of State of A.P. v. M. Madhusudhan Rao1, at para 30 has held as follows:
"30.

entities.text: State of A.P. v. M. Madhusudhan Rao1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Time and again, the object and importance of prompt lodging of the first information report has been highlighted.
Delay in lodging the first information report, more often than not, results in embellishment and exaggeration, which is a creature of an afterthought.

A delayed report not only gets bereft of the advantage of spontaneity, the danger of the introduction of a coloured (2008) 15 SCC 582 NC:
2024:KHC-D:8069 version, an exaggerated account of the incident or a concocted story as a result of deliberations and consultations, also creeps in, casting a serious doubt on its veracity.

Therefore, it is essential that the delay in lodging the report should be satisfactorily explained."
8.

Further, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar2, at para 18 has held as follows:
"18.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The above-mentioned decisions clearly demonstrate that this court has at numerous instances expressed concern over the misuse of section 498A IPC and the increased tendency of implicating relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes,
without analysing the long term ramifications of a trial on the complainant as well as the accused.

It is further manifest from the said judgments that false implication by way of general omnibus allegations made in (2022) 6 SCC 599 NC:
2024:KHC-D:8069 the course of matrimonial dispute, if left unchecked would result in misuse of the process of law.
Therefore, this court by way of its judgments has warned the courts from proceeding against the relatives and in-laws of the husband when no prima facie case is made out against them."

9. In the absence of any material that the petitioners- accused Nos.2 to 11 have subjected the defacto-complainant to cruelty both mentally and physically and also that there was a demand made to bring money from her parental home, the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate for the aforesaid offences is without any substance.
10. In view of the preceding analysis, the continuation of the criminal proceedings as against the petitioners-accused Nos.2 to 11 will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:8069 ORDER i. Criminal petition is allowed.
ii.

The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.11194/2023 pending on the file of the III Additional Civil Judge and JMFC Court at Hubballi arising out of crime No.42/2023 registered by Hubli-Dharwad City Women, Hubballi, for the offences punishable under Sections 498(A), 323, 504, 506 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, insofar as it relates to the petitioners-accused Nos.2 to 11 is hereby quashed.
